svg.title: The Pauli exclusion principle
svg.desc: Electrons drawn with arrows for spin up (ms = +1/2) or spin down (ms = −1/2) in the n = 1 and n = 2 shells. Allowed: one electron in n = 1 with either spin; two in n = 1 with opposite spins; and two opposite spins in n = 1 with a third electron, of either spin, in n = 2. Not allowed: two electrons in n = 1 with the same spin, or three electrons in n = 1, since n = 1 holds only two. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Pauli exclusion prevents duplicate sets of four quantum numbers
Arrows label spin projection, not spinning charged balls. A rejected trial never enters the occupied
state. Changing to 2s changes n, so a third electron can occupy it.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
